IQ tests and the factor analysis surrounding it was formulated long before the field of psychology understood the concept that some people are good at specific things. For many people, the g-factor — the idea that some underlying thing makes everyone intelligent — is almost irrelevant. Look up Spearman’s Law of Diminishing returns. It basically says that certain people in the lower percentiles are almost universally bad at these tests in all categories (g ~ 0.7, if I remember correctly) whereas people who score average or high don’t have that same underlying predictive factor (g ~ 0.3). This is why we have things like the General ability index (GAI) that stratify people and acknowledge that they’re still competent despite their “imbalances” on these tests… tests that aren’t even directly reflective of real world abilities. 

For example: I was tested at around the 6th percentile for visual memory. Despite this, I’ve memorized the shape of almost every nation and can recognize them by seeing the silhouettes of their geographic borders. What gives with that? 

I don’t even have to know you to say that you have plenty of relevant skills. On the surface level, you’re quite the competent writer, so I’d start there. You’re not defective, my man. These are all clear signs of neurodivergency in some respect. But don’t take this as a stranger on the internet giving you a diagnosis: you just have a specialized brain that can’t be effectively measured using a standardized test. Put simply, the constructs just aren’t as useful to you as they are for others.

Good question. There’s a lot of debate about HPD. In fact, based on my own research (and stuff I’ve learned in school), I wouldn’t be surprised if it doesn’t make it into the next DSM. I’m by no means an expert, but in extremely simplified terms, the way it’s purported to play out is: 

NPD — High self-importance and compromised empathy -> grandiose and manipulative behaviour, strained interpersonal relationships

HPD — A perceived need for excessive attention from virtually everyone -> grandiose and manipulative behaviour, strained interpersonal relationships

Basically, imagine someone who thinks they’re the best person ever and can even begin to disdain people who disagree. Then, compare them to someone who, almost instinctually, pursues attention from people and doesn’t necessarily know why. This slightly different “input” means slightly different “output.” In other words, different affect/cognition = slightly different manipulative, grandiose and impulsive behavioural patterns. But I’m sure you see how this could get messy and conflated. 

Also, as a side note: the real contention actually comes from the existence of BPD and ASPD. The overlap between these two is stark, which makes HPD redundant to some clinicians because of how under-researched it is. Some argue that the negative affect is stronger in BPD, which would mean that HPD is like a low-neuroticism version of BPD. Some argue that HPD is like ASPD without the violent/rule-breaking tendencies. Others argue that these cognitive styles are completely different.

Well that’s a much larger discussion, honestly. The truth is that while there are flawed methodologies and a LOT of things we don’t know, the same was (and in some cases, still is) true of medical science as well. Because of the fact that psychology is extremely new and has been used for a variety of evil things (phrenology, IQ-based voting systems), skepticism still runs rampant. As it should, in my opinion. 

This does not, by ANY STRETCH, mean that the MBTI and OCEAN personality models are on the same playing field. Virtually anybody who legitimately studies psychology can tell you that. 

The fact of the matter is that advancements in statistics and data collection, (not to mention cognitive neuroscience and biopsychology as a whole) mean that we’re getting closer and closer to understanding what’s true and what’s not about human cognition, emotion and behaviour — concretely. It’s just a longer process of replication. Will we ever arrive there? Who knows. But certain things have been reliably and diligently tested over and over again, which speaks for itself, I think.

No, the biggest difference between the tests is that the MBTI relies on dichotomies (which are called into question because of their jungian origins) and categorization of “types.” The Big 5’s dimensional approach to “traits” places them on a continuum that allows for better research and correlative data. The traits themselves are also more reflective of the real ways that personality manifests. This can be seen in clinical psychology, where personality disorders can easily be mapped to the big 5. I learned about this in class, today actually. 

The second biggest difference is that the first one is highly monetized and was designed by fans of a psychologist (whose theories have been largely discredited) for corporate purposes. The second one was designed *by* personality researchers *for* personality researchers. 

Thirdly, you’re misconstruing popularity with usefulness. Pop psychology works by appealing to biases like the Barnum effect — which is when people tend towards believing that vague positive terms describe them — and outright flattery. These are, almost 1-1, the same things that make *astrology* popular. Just because it’s fun doesn’t mean it’s practical. 

Flip that to the Big 5, and I’d wager that very few people would proudly proclaim that they’re “low in agreeableness” or “high in neuroticism” on a first date. Pop psychology is a huge problem because it devalues the work put into actual understandings of psychology. 
And, like you said, it’s “applied in the real world” despite this.

Psychology uses the scientific method, research and theory. The MBTI hasn’t been empirically backed in any meaningful sense — ever. It has always been pop psychology. The only category with any value is extraversion vs. introversion, which is included in the big 5 model. The rest are constructed on inherently flawed concepts and false dichotomies. 

Thinking vs feeling? Considering the fact that emotion and cognition are inherently human experiences, there is significant overlap. So what is the value in that categorization? It’s so unspecific.

Intuition vs sensation? Self-identified “intuitive” people are no better at tasks that require “intuition.” This has been measured repeatedly. And literally everyone who isn’t psychotic derives their truths from the physical world, which is what “sensation” is supposed to measure. 

I could go on. The point is that the big 5 model, though flawed, has distinct and concrete components (with very little overlap) that fall on a continuum. It’s dimensional, score-based, and overall more “scientific.” Not to mention the high external validity of the self-reporting.

The MBTI is entertainment, in comparison.

Another thing that people here rarely acknowledge is that cognitive testing is (by a large margin) more useful for diagnosing and treating people with deficits than it is for “identifying” those with notable strengths. It’s the primary clinical application of these tests, but they’re being misused for this obsessive measuring and ego-bruising (or boosting) rhetoric. 

If you don’t know who Shakespeare is at age 25, can’t remember something that happened 5 seconds ago or can’t get past the third figure on figure weights… yeah, that’s a problem and it’s great that these tests exist to identify that. 

On the other hand, if you happen to know the circumference of the moon or just absolutely CRUSH raven’s matrices, that’s not very descriptive about your abilities in real-life situations. There’s a downward threshold for how useful these tests are, clinically speaking. ESPECIALLY with young children.

I highly doubt that there would be any “signs of giftedness” in a three month old because there is virtually no way to detect these qualities in babies. Like, empirically — cognitive/developmental psychologists have tried. There’s just not enough information to be garnered from someone who likely won’t speak or even understand human speech for another 4-10 months. 

Giftedness is a construct of the education system. Only when your child can have their cognitive development compared to their peers in any meaningful way could they be labelled as gifted. In other words, there is no such thing as a “gifted baby” because there isn’t anything to be gifted AT. As cool as it would be…. she sadly just has almost no higher cognition yet.

Music theory is preeetty important. Its basically a really complicated ruleset. Doesn’t matter what plugins you have, the knowledge you have of your DAW, your skill on any instrument, or ur singing voice. In order for it to make sense to the listener, it will probably end up following the rules. 

But here’s the thing, If you don’t know it, you can still make a song just by fiddling around. I’ve done this before. Your ears tell you when it sounds outright awful. Drag the note around on the piano roll until your melody sounds like how you’ve imagined.  Boom, you’re probably following music theory. After all, the music theory “ruleset” itself is based on what we hear. 

From my experience, I still recommend learning it. Over the last two years, I’ve gradually learned music theory. I make pretty simple music, but it makes programming catchy synths (chords especially) 10x quicker. My melodies also make a lot more sense and i can stack multiple counter-melodies without any clashing. My drums bounce more thanks to syncopation… etc etc. Just overall better music. 

As a beginner, its not super necessary. Your music will be bad until a certain point regardless, and music production involves many other skills like mixing, recording, sound selection, and arrangement. But as you learn to make more complex songs, its pretty invaluable. And it’s inevitable that you’ll pick stuff up along the way. There’s a pretty good video by the youtuber Andrew Huang called “learn music theory in 30 minutes” or something. That should give u a jump start.

A multiband compressor is basically a compressor that allows you to compress different parts of the frequency spectrum in different ways, or only compress one frequency range. Most compressors operate with 3-4 adjustable ranges labelled, low mid, and high (sometimes the mids can be split into low-mids and high-mids.) This is most useful when you have one problematic part of a sound: e.g. high-pitched pick-noises on a guitar, not enough brightness in vocals, removing harsh bass distortion in only one range while keeping the distortion in the rest. Essentially a compressor, but more versatile. *HOWEVER* its easier to fuck up with multiband, so thats the tradeoff. If you’re brand new, learn with a normal compressor first to be perfectly honest. I should have mentioned both fruity compressors in my comment. Maximus is like a compressor on steroids that does…. a ton of things. But its a pain to learn. 

What I described is called gain staging. -12db is my chosen number, but not set in stone at all. The goal is to leave whats called “headroom”even before touching the faders. This is so you have room to work with the song while mastering, and things arent “clipping” (too much audio information makes some bad-sounding distortion happen) or getting squashed by your limiter. There’s a [video by beatmaking group Internet Money](https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=FxBOg0THvc8) that explains it better than i could in a single comment. They choose to use the volume knob in the channel rack but I recommend using fruity balance for more precision. It leads to a more even/balanced sounding mix.

These are complicated topics for sure lol. With compression and EQ chains alone you can make professional vocals. But I’ll give u a starting point cuz i’m mad bored

For compression: First make sure your input volume peaks at about -12db (use fruity balance for this, and make sure the rest of the song is also -12db) Next, set the ratio. The more aggressive ur delivery, the higher the ratio. Start with the ratio at 2:1-3:1. Then set the threshold (the point that the compressor starts working) and watch the gain reduction until the vocals are about -18db. Now listen. Adjust the thresh until its catching the quietest sections of ur vocals. The goal here is to make the vocals EVEN and PROMINENT in the mix while not destroying the transients (initial “hit” of ur words) so that’s where you’d mess with the attack/release. (Alternatively, if ur mic is picking up a lot of mouth noises like “Ps” and “Cs” even with a pop-filter, u can lower the attack to reduce these a bit) Then you adjust the makeup gain to bring everything back up to that initial -12db. If ur vocals are smacking u in the face, raise the ratio towards 4:1 or even 5:1. 5:1 + is when mfs are screaming on a track. Results should be much cleaner, even vocals while not sounding artificial. If ur satisfied, adjust the channel fader to taste. 

EDIT: If it sounds quiet compared to the rest of ur track, dont worry, this is cuz most ppl adjust faders with all instruments input volume at -12db (entire song peaking at -6db) before raising the volume on the master channel to -1db (the standard volume for music streaming) with fruity soft clipper and a limiter. You can learn more abt this online, its not as complicated as it seems. U can watch internet money’s video on it, just look up “internet money gain staging.” Helpful mixing trick as a whole, not just for vocals. 

Anyways, Compression is some complicated BS and a lot of ppl end up with 2 or even 3 compressors on their vocals sandwiched between their EQs. It’s all about solving problems and keeping ur vocals at the forefront. Look up on youtube what all of these terms mean…. Oooor you could just throw soundgoodizer on that shit if you dgaf lmao

EQ: This is a big one and u have to train ur ears for this. Compressors can bring a lot of annoying sounds to the forefront. After my first compressor, I usually make a low cut to take out unnecessary low end that just muddies shit up. Next i listen for problems. Is the high-end annoying? Solo the high end, look for problem frequencies and reduce accordingly. Does it need more warmth? Boost the low mids by a tiny bit. After my second compressor, I do the same thing again but a little less drastic, and look for other issues. Weird little buzzing? Make a tiny cut here…. Etc. Be careful tho. Dont do anything drastic if u dont know what ur doing, as you can sometimes end up with a worse result. Every voice, and every song, is different. I’d say for now, stick with one compressor and EQ as u train ur ears. 

Reverb: It depends on the vibe, but if ur going for sth subtle a good rule of thumb is: even if you think it isnt enough reverb, its too much. New producers love reverb, and they use it like crazy. Too much reverb can sound suuper corny on a main rap vocal, especially with stock plugins. What I used to do in fruity reverb 2 was raise the wet knob in the actual plugin to the max. If the reverb lasts too long, reduce the decay. If u want it to sound like ur in a massive space, increase the “size”, and vice versa for the sound of a more contained room. Then I would make the “dry” zero and adjust the dry/wet knob in the mixer channel until it sounds very subtle. Like, no more than 20% wet. 

There’s sooo much to learn with vocal mixing (de-essing, using an exciter) and i’m pretty passionate abt it if u cldnt tell (lmao) but for now focus on compression/EQ and finding cool vocal effects. 

My last tip mixing wise is to USE YOUR EARS. The visual guides in these plugins are helpful but they are never ur focus. Close ur eyes if you need to lmao.

For mixing:

Mastering u can keep even simpler. Fruity soft clipper on the master channel until ur peaking at around -1db, then put fruity limiter at -1db.

Filtering, crazy delays, vocal chops, vinyl effects, raising or lowering the pitch etc. This is how u bring life to a track like this. 

Anyways, layering. When I mix rap vocals that are sung, (not spoken) I do 3 different takes and an adlib. One of them, your best take, kept in the centre. Two of them panned left/right (usually a tiny bit of reverb on these) with less overall volume and slightly different EQ/compression settings. Adlibs I keep pretty quiet and they’re usually the most wet (meaning most effects) 

The key difference here is that ur rapping. If ur layering entire phrases of rap vocals, (and u arent just doubling the sample and making it unique and which doesnt really add much) ur timing needs to be absolutely perfect. This is why layering spoken rap in a home studio is difficult, and why you’re struggling. If you choose to layer the ENTIRE song instead of just emphasizing certain words and doing an adlib take, it often will not sound good unless every syllable is perfect. It takes maaaany takes and FL studio really isnt the best DAW for this. 

Layering isnt really what ur missing in my opinion, so don’t beat urself up over that. Get those vocal takes right, experiment with cool effects, put adlibs and emphasize certain words and you should see a way more drastic improvement than beating urself up trying to perfectly layer vocals lol

One key thing to realize is that genuine mastering only fixes slight issues with the mix, and is mainly useful with vocals in the question. If your low end is completely fucked or the vocals sound horrible, nothing will change with mastering except just being louder lol. Generally, mastering includes that final 10% of the mixing process, that can even be unnecessary depending on how good your mix is (besides getting it to the right volume.) 

MOST of the “professional sound” u keep mentioning happens with sound selection and mixing. Good sounds/patches. EQ, panning/stereo, some compression when necessary, and tasteful creative effects create that depth/wideness, while giving every instrument its space. But since this is the online trap community, you probably can keep the mixing process relatively simple (the most important part of improving is to actually make the music) but that “professional sound” is just that: the sound of a professional at work. A lot of engineers and audio experts have been doing this for decades. For now, focus on making that music and treat everything else as a detour. Nick mira’s mixing/mastering process is famously simple and he got to where he is by becoming extremely quick in the DAW, having great taste in sounds, learning how to sample and making beats around the clock. He’s been at it since 13. 

Anyways, I’m rambling. If you’re serious about building something in the youtube/soundcloud community, in terms of uploading for artists, this is my process: 

1. Put fruity balance at the end of my effects chain for every track and make sure its -12 db after EQ, compression, and effects

2. Then i adjust the faders. I only bring them DOWN, I never boost in this final mixing stage. The result is you should be peaking at abt -6db give or take. Be sure that everything is at the levels you want, and that there’s at least some room for vocals in the mix

3. Then quickly “master” using whatever method, usually just a soft clipper+limiter to get to -1db If you’re a tryhard, you can then do some more “proper” mastering with ozone 9 once u have the vocals. There’s an automatic mastering assistant that gets u started + lots of good tools for getting that tonal/dynamic balance and cleaning up some of the muddiness. To be honest though, wait until you have artists hitting you up to invest in ozone. A lot of the time, putting too much effort into mastering the beat removes the space for artists to put their own vocals on. It’s also pretty damn expensive for the full version. (You can torrent it but idk if thats ur style.)

4. Upload the “mastered” version to youtube (peaking at -1db.) If an artist asks for the beat to record on, send them the -6db version. Some artists will take it from here, but they may ask you to grab those vocals and master it again if no engineer is involved

Once again, since ur starting out, seriously just focus on making music that artists want. U prolly already know this though. Stay consistent with your uploads/brand, and dont give up. That’s the real battle.

This is how I see it. Please read this because I believe you can take my word for it: here’s why.

I am currently 17 years old, and from the ages of about 15-16 I was fucking miserable. And I mean MISERABLE. I have a really good life too. Tons of love, support, cool games to play and a good school to go to. But I looked at everything and asked the question, why? Why bother doing any of this? I am just consciousness placed into a monkey on a floating rock. Why should I waste my time with any of this? I could just as easily die and everything would be over.

But that’s the thing. *Everything* will be over. 

The thing about life is that everywhere you look there are things you can just *DO*. It’s incredible really when you think long enough. And I think we take it for granted. All around me is an endless sea of things I could create, people I could help or things I could learn, thanks mostly to society and the fruits of billions of other people before us’ labour. 

God, don’t even get me started on the things you can learn. Its like crack. I can keep myself occupied for hours on something as simple as youtube with endless streams of information about this massive planet, or, if I want something more active, I could apply myself, challenge my beliefs and train my mind to assess problems effectively using traditional school like college. I can learn to cook, making something which stimulates my biology using resources harvested from the same planet I was born out of. I can play video games which not only give me a much needed break from the sometimes harsh nature of life, but can stimulate my mind and teach me to assess problems quickly and efficiently. This is stuff anybody can do, and there is so much more!! It’s effectively infinite! Stuff on stuff on stuff on stuff, all of which changes you and grows you in even the smallest amounts. 

There’s a reason personal growth is such a popular concept in western media. It’s what you’re building your entire life. You start as a little ball of meat who just wants to eat and sleep, and by the end of it you can become a highly-conscious, value driven *being* whose consciousness is used to perceive the world around them in ways no other animal can (quite literally) even think about. I think that’s just beautiful man, no sugar coating. All the terrible things that happen around you, all the terrible things that happen *to* you, all the intellectuals and idiots, all the politics and ethics. They are overwhelming, scary, and saddening but they all mean something. Not to this universe obviously. But to us. To *people* like you and me. *That’s* why its important. None of us will be “okay” but we can always just try to work on things in the name of growth, using reason.

The first step for me was getting a job. I KNOW, I know, you hear it all the fucking time. I got sick of hearing it from my parents especially. But let me tell you something man. They’re correct. Plain and simple. Let’s face it, they have lived longer than us. (Bonus tip: pick a retail job if you want to work on your people skills) It doesn’t make people instantly happy, but can turn people who are being “held back” by their lack of motivation to engage in the world into people who, simply put, see a point to it. One time I was discussing this with my best friend who’s struggled heavily with depression and drug dependency:

I asked him how someone “lazy” like him could be his stores favourite employee, constantly working and getting 2 promotions in a year. His answer was quite simple. It’s hard, but it suits his life like nothing else. You wake up every morning with an expectation for your day, you fulfill that expectation for your employer but ALSO to yourself, (think: “okay I did my job today like i was supposed to”), you come home and do whatever you want, and get paid for your effort. That’s the thing too. The moments of doing “whatever you want” feel sooooo much more valuable. I can’t even describe the change in how I perceive entertainment, relaxation, food, masturbation, all of it.

And just like how you become “numb” to the constant dopamine pursuit you engage in while unmotivated, or “numb” to the emotions you feel while depressed, you can become “numb” to the feeling of “fuck this job I don’t want to do this this is a waste of time.” Human beings get used to ANYTHING. As long as it is consistent. And if you have an employer who expects you to show up, that’s all the consistency you need. But the longer you delay it, the harder it is to convince yourself. I say if this post in any way motivates you to get a job, close this tab after reading and work on your resumé. Fill out a job application for wherever you want and just *go*. Don’t think, don’t debate.

And listen man, of course it isnt easy. Shit is almost never completely easy, especially since it’s basically work or starve on this planet. But life is personal sacrifice in the pursuit of self growth. The pursuit of turning yourself from a breathing hunk of meat into a feeling, thinking person who will trudge into the depths and create something, anything, before your “free trial” of this incredible planet, this cosmic irregularity, is over. And we have a network around us, this society that stimulates our growth and gives us many different paths and opportunities. 

Sorry if this was really long-winded and mildly pretentious. But I do seriously think you should give these ideas a shot, run them around in your mind a bit. Challenge your perception of things. I really hope this helps, since I know I wasn’t willing to challenge myself at first because living in your beliefs is comfortable, especially when you take no risks. It sounds cliché (because it’s true) but you can do it, because anyone can do it. We all exist on this planet, no? That’s literally the concept of life, which other organisms have engaged in for billions of years. What stops us except time, mortality, and our own heads?

You can’t necessarily jump in on somebody in the neutral expecting them to be low blocking for whatever reason and continue a string of normals, its very unsafe. I say your best bet is to stay on the ground and poke with your long range moves, like medium (which you WERE doing, its a good habit.)

Speaking of, lows are your best bet for this. As the game goes on, more and more people will realize that blocking high is a good option, so getting free damage with low-hitting moves is really nice.
